assessment: The primary survey compares reported sunflower-oil use and other dietary habits among 161 international and 54 Ukrainian medical students aged 18–25. It reports oil-use frequencies rather than a refined-sunflower-oil intervention or swallowing outcome.

Olive oil in sealed plastic bags served as a breast imaging phantom for two beef specimens with different shapes. Ultrasound echogenicity and mammography do not measure dietary extra-virgin olive oil or swallowing.

The survey records self-reported use of unspecified olive oil as a cooking fat in two groups of medical students. Its findings give relative use frequencies and do not test oil intake against a swallowing outcome.
